caseAnalysis.title: Detention of HfA surgeons in Beta Town after announced closure
caseAnalysis.summary: Shared case materials only; no role card identifies our side. Nine Swiss HfA surgeons are confined to their residence in Beta Town by armed tribespeople. This followed HfA's announcement that it would end Beta Town operations and redeploy to Gamma. HfA reports that staff cannot leave until an agreement on health service maintenance is reached with tribal leaders. The tribal chief demands that hospital activities restart, that HfA commit to staying, and that HfA reinforce the measles response. HfA states its long-term presence is not viable, keeps a strict no-ransom policy and wants release before discussing the dispute. Donors Germany and Switzerland reportedly mandate the move to Gamma. The Swiss Ambassador will ask Bern about special funds for minimal services. Police and government defer to tribal leaders.

issues.text: No role card or private instructions were supplied. The materials contain prompts for both an HfA-supporting negotiator and the Tribal Leader, so our side cannot be established.
HfA says the move to Gamma is firm and donor-mandated, yet it asked about compromises on Beta Town programs for the coming months and showed willingness to seek a compromise.

Sequencing conflict: HfA insists on release before discussing the dispute, while the tribal chief bars contact with staff until an amicable resolution is reached and the police link their involvement to a health-services agreement.
Swiss special funds are not approved. The Ambassador committed only to communicate with Bern about them.

immediate.text: HfA reports that its staff are confined to their residence and cannot leave until an agreement with tribal leaders on health service maintenance is reached. The tribal chief has told the delegation to wait at its hotel for further guidance.

actors.text: The tribal chief demands that hospital activities restart quickly, with HfA committing to continue operations, and that HfA reinforce the local measles response.
The HfA delegation says its long-term presence is not viable. It holds a no-ransom policy and wants release first.
The Swiss Ambassador warns against paying ransoms. He will ask Bern about special funds for minimal services, including measles support.
The German Ambassador says compromise decisions are beyond her authority and rest with Berlin. She opposes diverting humanitarian aid to development.
The police chief says police will not intervene. Police will step in to restore peace once a health-services agreement is reached.
The Minister of Health says the release largely rests with tribal leaders and that government interference might escalate tensions.

tension.text: The tribal demand for continued operations conflicts with HfA's stated donor-mandated, funding-driven exit and its release-first stance.

background.text: HfA announced that it is transferring the Country Director and Beta Town personnel to Gamma City. The guard representatives blame the sudden departure and defer the release decision to tribal leaders.

uncertainty.text: HfA fears ransom demands and unpredictable action by local guards if no prompt solution is found.
The police chief views resolution as improbable amid labor disagreements.
Our represented side and its authority are unknown.

response_branches.text: If the chief insists on a permanent commitment, test whether a time-limited minimal-services commitment would suffice, while noting that HfA calls long-term presence not viable.
If money is demanded, keep the discussion on service funding rather than payment, given HfA's no-ransom policy.
If guard compensation is raised, refer to HfA's commitment to consult headquarters.

Assumes tribal leaders accept less than a full commitment to stay.
